slides.title: Type mean(L) and median(L)
slides.question: A data set is $3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 9, 48$. How do its mean and median compare?
slides.caption: No graph needed. Type the list, then ask for both. The single $48$ drags the mean up and leaves the median alone.

slides.title: Type histogram(L)
slides.question: Which best describes the distribution of the data set $3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 9, 48$?
slides.caption: The same ten numbers, drawn. One long tail to the right is what "skewed right" looks like.

slides.title: Type boxplot(L)
slides.question: What is the median of the data set $3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 9, 48$?
slides.caption: The line inside the box is the median. The box holds the middle half of the data.
